parts.text: Explain why there are few plants on the floor of a dense forest.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• trees block the light (1)
• low light intensity (1)
• less photosynthesis so plants cannot grow (1)

parts.text: Explain how an increase in the number of foxes could affect the population of rabbits.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• more rabbits eaten / more predation (1)
• rabbit population decreases (1)

parts.text: Explain why a student should use many quadrats rather than one when estimating a population.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• one quadrat may not be representative (1)
• a mean of many gives a more reliable estimate (1)

parts.text: Explain why a transect is used rather than random quadrats to study plants from the edge of a pond into a field.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• there is a gradient of conditions / change in abiotic factor (1)
• transect shows how distribution changes with distance (1)

parts.text: Explain why the population of a species of moss is larger on the north side of a wall than on the south side.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• north side is shaded / less light (1)
• more damp / less evaporation (1)
• moss needs moist conditions (1)

parts.text: Explain why high biodiversity makes an ecosystem more stable.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• many food webs / alternative food sources (1)
• loss of one species has less effect (1)

parts.text: Explain how competition between two plant species can affect their distribution.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• both need the same resources / light / water / minerals (1)
• the better competitor grows more (1)
• the other is excluded or found only where the first cannot grow (1)

parts.text: Describe how energy passes along a food chain.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• light energy captured by producers in photosynthesis (1)
• stored as chemical energy in biomass (1)
• passed to consumers when they eat (1)
• some lost at each level as heat (1)

parts.text: Describe the shape of a pyramid of energy and explain why it always has this shape.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• always a true pyramid / wider at the base (1)
• each level is smaller than the one below (1)
• energy lost at each transfer (1)

parts.text: Describe the role of decomposers in an ecosystem.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• break down dead organisms / waste (1)
• by releasing enzymes / saprotrophic nutrition (1)
• return minerals / nutrients to the soil (1)
• release carbon dioxide by respiration (1)

parts.text: Describe how substances such as carbon pass through a food chain.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• carbon compounds in producers are eaten by consumers (1)
• used in growth / passed up the chain and returned by respiration and decay (1)

parts.text: Describe how a pyramid of biomass is constructed.

• collect / sample organisms at each trophic level (1)
• dry them / find dry mass (1)
• draw bars proportional to mass per unit area (1)
• producers at the bottom (1)

rows.answer:

• energy used in respiration / lost as heat (1)
• energy used for movement (1)
• some material not eaten / bones / roots (1)
• some energy lost in faeces / not digested (1)
• energy lost in urine / excretion (1)

• energy lost at each level (1)
• too little energy left to support another level (1)

parts.text: Explain why it is more efficient for humans to eat plants than to eat meat.

• fewer trophic levels (1)
• less energy lost (1)
• more food / energy per area of land (1)

parts.text: Describe how carbon is cycled between the atmosphere, plants and animals.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to six of the following:
• plants absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis (1)
• carbon becomes part of carbohydrates / plant tissue (1)
• animals eat plants and carbon passes along the food chain (1)
• respiration by plants and animals releases carbon dioxide (1)
• decomposers break down dead organisms and waste (1)
• decomposers respire releasing carbon dioxide (1)
• combustion of fossil fuels / wood releases carbon dioxide (1)
• fossil fuels form from dead organisms over millions of years (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Describe the roles of bacteria in the nitrogen cycle and how plants obtain nitrogen.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to six of the following:
• nitrogen-fixing bacteria convert nitrogen gas into ammonium / nitrogen compounds (1)
• in root nodules of legumes or in soil (1)
• decomposers break down proteins / urea into ammonium (1)
• nitrifying bacteria convert ammonium to nitrite then nitrate (1)
• plants absorb nitrate through roots (1)
• nitrate used to make amino acids / proteins (1)
• denitrifying bacteria convert nitrate to nitrogen gas (1)
• lightning also fixes nitrogen (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Explain why growing peas or beans can improve the nitrogen content of soil.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• peas and beans are legumes (1)
• they have root nodules (1)
• containing nitrogen-fixing bacteria (1)
• which convert nitrogen gas into ammonium / nitrogen compounds (1)
• the plant uses these to make amino acids / proteins (1)
• when the plants die or are ploughed in, decomposers release ammonium (1)
• nitrifying bacteria convert ammonium to nitrate (1)
• nitrate is then available for the next crop (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Explain how cutting down and burning a forest affects the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• trees remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis (1)
• fewer trees so less carbon dioxide is absorbed (1)
• burning releases carbon dioxide (1)
• carbon stored in wood is released quickly (1)
• decomposers respire as they break down remaining wood / roots (1)
• releasing more carbon dioxide (1)
• so the carbon dioxide concentration in the air rises (1)
• carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas / contributes to global warming (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text:
Explain why ploughing and draining waterlogged fields can improve the nitrogen content of soil.

Your answer should include clear links between the points you make.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• ploughing / draining adds air / oxygen to the soil (1)
• aerobic conditions favour nitrifying bacteria (1)
